title: Trip lookup: a heartbeat trip covers the identification, skipped by the type filter
description: This trip's type is set to heartbeat rather than normal. The covering-trip lookup's SQL filters on type = 'normal', so this trip is invisible to the query even though its [start_date, end_date] window genuinely covers the identification's timestamp. The covering lookup that the identification consumer and the trip-end consumer both use must apply this same type filter. Must prove: the identification behaves exactly as O12d (unlinked, no write) despite a trip whose window covers it. Must NOT change: the asset assignee must stay untouched; the trip's own assignee must also stay untouched, since the trip is never a candidate in the first place.

driver_identifications.note: timestamp genuinely falls inside this trip's window, but the trip's non-normal type must exclude it from the lookup
